reviewer: Kimi independent actual visual comparison of the exact 65x67 source PNG, enlarged existing source-page 05 and its native crop, complete unchanged 2048x2048 raw RGBA, native-resolution collar/shoulder crop, full white/cyan/alpha review sheet and unchanged naiwa.png mascot reference; checked bald crown and side hair, brows, upper-lip-only moustache, one mouth, uniform/shoulder/collar decorations, pose, crop, lighting, collar fit, complete card/note/backplate and visible transparency.

entries.positive_observation: The high bald crown with short brown hair at the sides and back, brown eyebrows and distinct narrow brown upper-lip moustache remain. The moustache does not extend into chin or jaw hair; there is one serious closed mouth and no added headgear or glasses. The three-quarter head turn and gaze toward viewer left, nearly frontal shoulders, chest-up crop and warm directional cheek modeling are retained. The dark olive uniform keeps two red-and-gold collar patches, visible gold shoulder trim with one prominent shoulder board, one pale blue-white neck ribbon and one silver-toned cross-shaped pendant at the throat; no additional medal was added. Native collar inspection shows coherent front/back cloth contact around a short broad neck, with no long yellow column, pinching, clipping or cream bib. The complete tilted dark frame, opaque light warm-gray/gray-olive photographic backplate, overlapping warm-cream note with gray upper marks and mostly blank lower paper, and small dark right-edge tab remain. Full white/cyan inspection shows a genuine transparent exterior without visible interior holes, lost backing or working-matte halo.
entries.alpha_decision: Accept native RGBA extrema 0..254 after actual white/cyan/alpha inspection; no source-alpha replacement was performed or needed, and 252-254 values alone were not treated as defects.
entries.visible_limitations: At 65x67 the exact collar symbols, pendant details, fine ribbon colors and partly occluded shoulder embroidery cannot be resolved completely; only visible forms, colors and placements were compared, without claiming exact rank symbols or hidden-side construction. Existing note marks remain indistinct visual groups rather than readable text.
